hints.content: $\displaystyle \int_{-4}^{5} f(x) \, dx$ is the net area between $f(x)$ and the $x$-axis from $x = -4$ to $x = 5$.

Let's look at the graph from $x = -4$ to $x = 5$:

![Function f is graphed. The x-axis goes from negative 8 to 5. The graph consists of a smooth curve. The curve starts at (negative 4, 0), moves downward to a relative minimum in quadrant 3, moves upward through (0, 0) to a relative maximum in quadrant 1, moves downward and ends at (5, 0). 2 regions are shaded between the curve and the x-axis. The region below the x-axis between x-intercepts negative 4 and 0 has area negative 6. The region above the x-axis between x-intercepts 0 and 5 has area 4.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/f22bd0e54182bbad1c6b77deca24bb144b60a9e0)

Remember that whenever a region is below the $x$-axis, the definite integral is negative.

$\begin{align}&\phantom{=}\displaystyle \int_{-4}^5 f(x) \, dx 
\\\\
&= \displaystyle \int_{-4}^{0} f(x) \, dx + \displaystyle \int_{0}^5 f(x) \, dx 
\\\\
&= (\maroonE{-6})+\blueE{4} 
\\\\
&=-2
\end{align}$
